newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: SanMig in "backdoor" listing for realty arm.
newsitem.headline: SanMig in "backdoor" listing for realty arm.

text.p: Food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp on Thursday undertook a virtual "backdoor" listing of its property arm by merging it with an inactive listed poultry subsidiary.
The company told the Philippine Stock Exchange San Miguel Properties Philippines Inc (SMPPI) would be merged with Monterey Farms Corp.
Monterey in turn would spin off its meat and livestock operations to a new company.
"The merger will provide San Miguel's real estate business with a vehicle to access the equity capital market in the future to finance its redevelopment projects," a San Miguel statement said.
Monterey will remain the suviving entity. The merger is expected to be completed within three to four months.
A backdoor listing refers to companies taking over listed firms and gaining access to the equities market without going through the cumbersome requirements for listing.

At present, SMPPI has total real estate assets worth 15.2 billion pesos, while Monterey, which has a vast processing plant in the industrial Cavite province, owns property assets worth 1.2 billion pesos.
SMPPI has a number of commercial real estate projects in the country, including joint ventures with Kuok Properties Philippines Inc, HongKong Land Holdings Ltd and Jardine Davies Inc.
Its projects include office buidlings and middle-cost housing projects.

Its major project will be the redevelopment of its six-hectare head office site into a mixed-use complex to be consist of office and residential towers, a hotel, commercial and leisure establishments.

San Miguel's statement said it had assured Monterey workers that its meat and livestock businesses, including all operating assets and liabilities would be spun off into a new separate company called Monterey Foods Corp.
"The meat business continues to perform well and growth prospects for Monterey, an industry leader with strong brands, remain excellent," it added.
Monterey posted a rebound in its operating income in 1996 to 116 million pesos from a loss of 123 million in 1995.
